title: Sentinel regression shield: slice-aware canary & A/B eval gates with auto rollback orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
We have recurring production regressions introduced by configuration and model swaps that only surface on small traffic slices or specific customers. Existing canary gates run aggregate evals which frequently miss slice-level regressions, and rollback is partially manual (on-call toggles routes), delaying mitigation and increasing customer impact.

Goal:
Build a Sentinel Regression Shield that enforces slice-aware canary + A/B eval gates and an automated rollback orchestration layer. The system should:
- Evaluate quality metrics across pre-defined and discovered slices (LLM hallucination rate, BLEU/ROUGE proxies, perplexity, latency, token cost).
- Trigger automatic rollback when SLOs or slice-specific thresholds degrade beyond configurable tolerances.
- Integrate with our rollout controller to shift traffic and with PagerDuty/Slack for notifications and postmortem artifacts.
- Provide clear visibility (dashboards & runbooks) and a safe opt-out path for emergency overrides.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Sentinel Evaluator: a near-real-time eval harness that samples production traffic (bounded sample rate) and replays to candidate variant(s) in isolated evaluation pools. It computes per-slice metrics and risk scores.
2) Slice definitions: a combination of static slices (customer tier, region, model family) and dynamic discovery (response template clusters, prompt fingerprints). Slices can be marked critical.
3) Gate engine: policy rules that evaluate metric deltas vs baseline. Policies support: absolute thresholds, relative drift, and Bayesian posterior checks for low-sample slices.
4) Rollback orchestrator: when Gate engine trips, orchestrator will: (a) shift traffic away from candidate variant using weighted routing (canary->baseline), (b) mark rollout as failed and stop further rollouts, (c) create remediation ticket and attach eval artifacts. Orchestrator also supports staged partial rollbacks and automatic follow-up checks after rollback.
5) Observability: new dashboards (canary-eval-overview, slice-detail), synthetic probes, and a forensics bundle (sampled prompts + responses + eval diffs) attached to incidents.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Implementation spike and API design for Sentinel Evaluator and Gate Engine. Define slice taxonomy and sampling policy. (Owners: Marco + Priya)
- Week 2: Build teaser harness to replay sampled traffic against a 'shadow' model and compute baseline deltas. Expose minimal metrics to DataDog. (Owner: Marco)
- Week 3: Gate engine prototype with absolute + relative thresholds, include Bayesian check for low-sample slices. Integrate as a webhook-based decision service consumed by rollout controller. (Owner: Ethan)
- Week 4: Rollback orchestrator implementation: routing API calls, small-step rollback, and incident creation. Wire into Slack + PagerDuty runbooks. (Owner: Sofia)
- Week 5: End-to-end test and internal canary using non-critical models. Create dashboards and runbooks. (Owner: Aisha)

Acceptance criteria:
- Sentinel Evaluator samples production traffic at target sample rates (configurable) without measurable latency impact on live requests.
- Gate engine evaluates all configured slices and returns a decision within SLA (<= 2s decision latency for canary checks).
- Automatic rollback reverses traffic to baseline within 60s of a gate 'fail' signal for full-canary failures; supports partial-weight rollbacks for noisy signals.
- Post-rollback forensics bundle generated automatically and linked to the rollback incident/ticket.
- No false positive rollback in internal canary test (false-positive rate < 2% over 2 weeks of simulated noisy signals).

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for metric computation and Bayesian delta logic.
- Integration tests with local rollout controller and mock traffic.
- Staging canary run against historical traces (replay) and synthetic adversarial prompts to validate slice detection.
- Internal controlled rollout (1% traffic) for 72h with manual override enabled.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Evaluator sampling adds cost and potential privacy exposure. Mitigation: strict PII redaction in replay path and sample rate quotas per customer. Security review required.
- Risk: Gate sensitivity too high -> frequent rollbacks. Mitigation: implement hysteresis windows, require sustained degradation over N minutes or Bayesian posterior beyond confidence.
- Risk: Low-sample slices lead to noisy decisions. Mitigation: use Bayesian checks and aggregate across similar slices; support fallthrough to manual review for critical slices.

Operational runbook (short):
- Alert: Canary Gate Failure (severity high) -> Orchestrator created rollback ticket and posted to #oncall-rollouts.
- On-call action: confirm rollback, validate forensics bundle, and if rollback is incorrect, escalate to infra on-call to re-route traffic.
- Post-incident: attach canary artifact to release blocklist and schedule root cause analysis with model owners.

Dependencies:
- ENG-6123 (cohort-eval-auto-rollback-controller) for prior rollback abstractions
- ENG-5291 for canary eval automation primitives
- infra: routing API (tickets exist)
- security: PII redaction audit (will coordinate)

Deliverables:
- Sentinel service + Gate engine (k8s svc + API)
- Rollback orchestrator extension to rollout-controller
- Dashboards: canary-eval-overview, slice-health, rollback-events
- Runbook + PagerDuty playbook
- Confluence design doc and public SDK shim for partners

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/ENG-8740+Sentinel+Design (draft)
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1458
- Dashboard (staging): https://datadog.com/dashboards/SEn-Canary-Eval (placeholder)

Notes:
- This ticket focuses on the engineering plumbing and automation. UX for model owners (fine-grained policy config UI) will be a follow-up PM + design ticket.
- We must ensure the rollback path cannot be triggered by unauthorized agents; Gate engine calls require mTLS and JWT verification.
